newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish banks could merge after April 29 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Swedish banks could merge after April 29 - paper.

text.p: A widely flagged merger between Swedish banks S-E-Banken and state-controlled Nordbanken is still in the cards, but will not take place until after April 29, a Swedish newspaper said on Monday.
"According to sources close to the merger efforts, no new developments should be expected until after S-E-Banken's general shareholders meeting on April 29," business daily Dagens Industri said.

The newspaper said that S-E-Banken shares rose late on Friday on rumours that merger talks would be held over the weekend. Nordbanken's management had also booked a meeting for Saturday, the newspaper said.
On Friday S-E-Banken closed up 4.3 percent on the week at a record 84.5 crowns because of a fresh round of speculation that a merger with Nordbanken was imminent.
"The last word has not been spoken about S-E-Banken and Nordbanken," said Fiba analyst Jan Dworsky.
Shares in both banks have risen since last autumn on speculation of a merger as the sector undergoes restructuring.

Merger talks between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken, which is 59 percent owned by the state, collapsed in early February with no clear reason given although it was believed to be over management differences.

Since then, Swedish banks Swedbank and Foreningsbanken announced they would merge to become the country's second largest bank, called ForeningsSparbanken after Handelsbanken which bought mortgage bank Stadshypotek.
"I think a merger between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken will be the last big new structure. It's coming," said one Stockholm-based analyst who asked not to be named.
At 1550 S-E-Banken traded at 82 crowns, down 2.5 while Nordbanken had risen three crowns to 269.
